subproblem.title: Graph inequality on a single null-measurable L-Lipschitz graph piece, for arbitrary [0,∞]-valued integrands
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, P ∈ G(N,n) with orthogonal projection p := Grassmannian.project P, L ≥ 0, A ⊆ ℝ^N an L-Lipschitz graph over P (|(y − z) − p(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ A) that is H^n-null-measurable, H^n = μHE[n], and g : ℝ^N → [0,∞] arbitrary (not necessarily measurable). Then ∫⁻_A g dH^n ≤ (1 + L²)^{n/2} ∫⁻_{P.plane} (Σ_{y∈A, p(y)=a} g(y)) dH^n(a), where ∫⁻ is the lower Lebesgue integral and the inner sum is the [0,∞]-valued sum (tsum) of g over the subtype {y : y ∈ A ∧ p(y) = a}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (P : Grassmannian N n) (L : ℝ) (A : Set (Euclidean N)) (g : Euclidean N → ℝ≥0∞), 0 ≤ L → (∀ y ∈ A, ∀ z ∈ A, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖) → NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) → ∫⁻ y in A, g y ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + L ^ 2) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)) * ∫⁻ a in (P.plane : Set (Euclidean N)), (∑' y : {y : Euclidean N // y ∈ A ∧ Grassmannian.project P y = a}, g y) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3 (fibres of one piece), 4 (Borel simple integrands) and 5 (arbitrary g) of the parent proof (step B6 (iii)–(iv) of the proof of Simon 8.5.9), for a single graph piece A. Uses the sibling results graph_hausdorff_bound (Lean: Submission.intcpt_graph_hausdorff_le_projection; H^n(S) ≤ (1 + L²)^{n/2} H^n(p(S)) for every L-Lipschitz graph S over P) and graph_projection_null_measurable (Lean: Submission.intcpt_graph_projection_nullMeasurableSet; p(S) is H^n-null-measurable for every H^n-null-measurable L-Lipschitz graph S over P). Notation: H^n := μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, an outer measure, so H^n(S) is defined for every set S); p := Grassmannian.project P, the orthogonal projection onto the n-plane P.plane = range p; it is linear (p = P.projectionLinearMap), symmetric (Grassmannian.projectionLinearMap_isSymmetric) and idempotent (Grassmannian.project_project). A set S ⊆ ℝ^N is an L-Lipschitz graph over P when |(y − z) − p(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ S; every subset of such a set is again one. Write C := ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2}), μ := H^n and, for a ∈ ℝ^N, F(a) := Σ_{y∈A, p(y)=a} g(y), the [0,∞]-valued sum (tsum) of g over the subtype {y : y ∈ A ∧ p(y) = a}.

1. Preliminaries. p is injective on A: if y, z ∈ A and p(y) = p(z), then p(y − z) = 0 and the graph inequality forces y − z = 0. P.plane = range p is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed and Borel (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), and p(y) ∈ P.plane for every y.

2. Pieces of a simple function. Fix a Borel simple function s : ℝ^N → [0,∞] (MeasureTheory.SimpleFunc; its values may be ∞) with s ≤ g pointwise. For each c in the finite range of s put E_c := s⁻¹{c} (Borel) and A_c := E_c ∩ A. Each A_c ⊆ A is an L-Lipschitz graph over P and is H^n-null-measurable (a Borel set intersected with a null-measurable one). By graph_projection_null_measurable, p(A_c) is H^n-null-measurable; by graph_hausdorff_bound, μ(A_c) ≤ C·μ(p(A_c)).

3. The simple integral over A. By the definition of the integral of a simple function with respect to the restricted measure μ⌞A (SimpleFunc.lintegral s (μ⌞A) = Σ_c c·(μ⌞A)(s⁻¹{c})) and Measure.restrict_apply for the Borel sets E_c, SimpleFunc.lintegral s (μ⌞A) = Σ_c c·(μ⌞A)(E_c) = Σ_c c·μ(A_c). (No measurability of A is needed for this identity.)

4. Transfer to the plane. For each c, c·μ(A_c) ≤ c·C·μ(p(A_c)) = C·∫⁻ c·1_{p(A_c)} dμ, the equality by lintegral_indicator_const₀ (p(A_c) is null-measurable by step 2). Summing over the finite range and using finite additivity of the integral for the a.e.-measurable functions c·1_{p(A_c)} (lintegral_finsetSum', AEMeasurable.indicator₀): Σ_c c·μ(A_c) ≤ C·Σ_c ∫⁻ c·1_{p(A_c)} dμ = C·∫⁻ Φ dμ, where Φ(a) := Σ_c c·1_{p(A_c)}(a).

5. Pointwise comparison with the fibre sum: Φ(a) ≤ 1_{P.plane}(a)·F(a) for every a ∈ ℝ^N. (i) If a ∉ p(A), then a ∉ p(A_c) for every c (as A_c ⊆ A), so Φ(a) = 0. (ii) If a = p(y₀) with y₀ ∈ A, then for every c: a ∈ p(A_c) iff s(y₀) = c (if a = p(y) with y ∈ A_c ⊆ A, injectivity gives y = y₀ and so s(y₀) = c; conversely y₀ ∈ A_c when s(y₀) = c). Hence Φ(a) = Σ_c [s(y₀) = c]·c = s(y₀), because s(y₀) lies in the range of s (Finset.sum_ite_eq). Moreover s(y₀) ≤ g(y₀) ≤ F(a), since y₀ is one term of the fibre {y ∈ A : p(y) = a} (ENNReal.le_tsum), and a = p(y₀) ∈ P.plane.

6. Bound for s. By steps 3–5, lintegral_mono (which needs no measurability) and lintegral_indicator for the Borel set P.plane: SimpleFunc.lintegral s (μ⌞A) = Σ_c c·μ(A_c) ≤ C·∫⁻ Φ dμ ≤ C·∫⁻ 1_{P.plane}·F dμ = C·∫⁻_{P.plane} F dμ.

7. Arbitrary g. By definition (MeasureTheory.lintegral), the lower Lebesgue integral ∫⁻_A g dμ = ∫⁻ g d(μ⌞A) is the supremum of SimpleFunc.lintegral s (μ⌞A) over all Borel simple functions s ≤ g (rw [MeasureTheory.lintegral]; iSup₂_le). Each of these is at most C·∫⁻_{P.plane} F dμ by step 6, so ∫⁻_A g dH^n ≤ ofReal((1 + L²)^{n/2})·∫⁻_{P.plane} (Σ_{y∈A, p(y)=a} g(y)) dH^n(a). No layer-cake formula is needed, and simple functions taking the value ∞ are allowed. ∎
proof_key_steps: p is injective on A and P.plane = range p is Borel.
For a Borel simple s ≤ g with level sets E_c: A_c := E_c ∩ A has μ(A_c) ≤ C μ(p(A_c)) and p(A_c) null-measurable (siblings).
SimpleFunc.lintegral s (μ⌞A) = Σ_c c μ(A_c) ≤ C ∫⁻ Σ_c c·1_{p(A_c)} dμ.
Pointwise Σ_c c·1_{p(A_c)}(a) ≤ 1_{P.plane}(a)·Σ_{y∈A, p(y)=a} g(y), by injectivity of p on A and s ≤ g.
Take the supremum over Borel simple s ≤ g (definition of the lower integral).

audit.reason: The exact contract includes arbitrary ENNReal-valued g. The proof correctly applies both declared siblings to simple-function level sets, integrates their null-measurable projected indicators, compares pointwise with the subtype fibre sum, and takes the defining lower-integral supremum. Infinite values are allowed, and no measurability of g or circular reliance is introduced.
